A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the edge and arc disjoint Menger problems can both be solved in linear time in planar undirected and directed graphs, respectively.
the arc disjoint Menger version is the first problem in planar graphs which has an asymptotically optimal algorithm in both directions, i.e., in the directed case as well as in the undirected case.

we have solved to optimality the arc disjoint Menger and the edge disjoint Menge problem for planar directed graphs, while for the arc disjoint Menge problem we have improved the running time of the best known algorithms from \bf O (n log n) to \bf O (m).
The main takeaway from our work is that
for planar graphs, arc disjointness is easier to deal with than edge disjointness.

the arc disjoint Menger algorithm is a natural and elegant extension of the vertex disjoint version in planary graphs, and that it can be solved in linear time using only the same tools as for the vertex disjoint version.
the planarity of a directed graph is not only sufficient but also necessary for an asymptotically optimal solution of the arc disjoint Menger's problem.
